papers.title: Additively Produced Ti-6Al-4V Osteosynthesis Devices Meet the Requirements for Tensile Strength and Fatigue
papers.abstract: The purpose of this study was to estimate the peak stresses in a laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) additive-manufactured (AM) osteosynthesis plate during physiological loading and establish if the mechanical properties of LPBF titanium alloy were suitable for this use case. Finite element models of subject-specific osteosynthesis plates for a cohort of 28 patients were created and used to calculate the peak maximum principal stresses during physiological loading, which was estimated to be 166 MPa twelve weeks post-operatively. All specimens were LPBF additively manufactured in Ti-6Al-4V alloy. ISO compliant tests were performed for tensile and fatigue, respectively. Fatigue testing was performed for specimens that had been heat-treated only and those that had been heat-treated and polished. The Upper Yield Stress was 1012.5 ± 19.2 MPa. The fatigue limit was 227 MPa for heat-treated only specimens and increased to 286 MPa for heat-treated and polished specimens. The finite element predicted stresses were below the experimentally established limits of yield and fatigue. The tensile and fatigue properties of heat-treated LPBF Ti-6Al-4V are therefore sufficient to meet the mechanical requirements of osteosynthesis plates. Polishing is recommended to improve fatigue resistance.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估增材制造Ti-6Al-4V接骨板是否满足生理载荷下的力学要求。
summary_zh.method: 对28例患者个性化接骨板进行有限元分析，并对热处理和抛光后的试样进行拉伸和疲劳测试。
summary_zh.result: 热处理试样疲劳极限227 MPa，抛光后提升至286 MPa，均高于预测的生理应力。
summary_zh.validation: 通过ISO标准拉伸和疲劳测试验证力学性能。

summary_en.motivation: To determine whether additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V osteosynthesis plates can withstand physiological loading after post-processing.
summary_en.method: Finite element models of patient-specific plates were used to predict peak stresses, and tensile and fatigue tests were conducted on heat-treated and polished specimens.
summary_en.result: The fatigue limit increased from 227 MPa (heat-treated only) to 286 MPa (heat-treated and polished), both exceeding the predicted physiological stress of 166 MPa.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical validation was performed using ISO-compliant tensile and fatigue testing.

summary_en.motivation: To develop a tribo-efficient novel nanostructured silica coating for additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V substrates.
summary_en.method: Silica coatings were synthesized on LPBF Ti-6Al-4V via thermal degradation of PMMA templates.
summary_en.result: The coated surfaces exhibited improved wear resistance and reduced friction coefficients compared to uncoated samples.
summary_en.validation: Tribological performance was validated through pin-on-disc wear tests and surface characterization.

papers.title: Effect of 3 wt% Cu on the Microstructure and Hardness of a Ti-10Ta-1.6Zr Alloy
papers.abstract: Alloys of Ti-10Ta-1.6Zr (wt%) with and without 3 wt% Cu made by arc-melting, heat-treated in two stages and quenched to have α + β microstructures were studied. These alloys were studied for potential replacement of Ti-6Al-4V alloys because Ta and Zr are more biocompatible than Al and V, and copper was added for potential antimicrobial properties. The heat-treated samples were investigated by SEM-EDX, transmission Kikuchi diffraction (TKD) and XRD. When studied at a higher magnification, the heat-treated alloys revealed a bi-lamellar microstructure, consisting of broad α lamellae and β transformed to fine α' lamellae with various orientations. The fraction β transformed to fine α' lamellae was higher in the alloy with Cu than that without Cu. Furthermore, copper was found to lower the solubility of tantalum in the β. The hardest alloy was the heat-treated alloy containing Cu, albeit with a wide standard deviation, probably due to the high fraction of martensitically transformed β.
